focus: deepseek-06: cli-deem through the custom provider: the failure side

label: No guard refuses loopback or plain-HTTP endpoints; the dispatch check only requires an endpoint value to exist, the CLI accepts any override, and the skill's HTTPS line is advisory; the recorded matrix sent http://127.0.0.1:9
The bearer must resolve before any byte is sent (env JEV_API_KEY then stored custom key, else exit 3); Deem performs no auth read; matrix order: no endpoint exit 2, endpoint-no-key exit 3

Exit map against Deem: no endpoint 2; no key 3; refused 4; 400/413 -> 1; 500 -> 4; stub noul without --value 0; noul/score with --value KeyError 1; choice --value 0; run --value 2 after billed call; no default-value path
auth status --provider custom exits 0 with an env key regardless of the server; it must never be the Deem availability check

Field gap settled both sides (inferred): jev sends criteria (dict/list) for choice/score while Deem reads options/levels; jev reads noul/score while Deem returns value/level; choice answer key matches for an untranslated choice
Verdict: not a thin wrapper; a separate Node client (or a translator that pays a fake secret and a vendored edit) - the client wins on failure side; run-only passthrough is a raw client not a wrapper
Do not widen the dispatch guard: loopback HTTP testing is legitimate and a direct Deem client never uses --provider custom; the client design removes the path instead
